answer: A lagoon-side botanical garden gives each agent one numbered garden bed to tend. The steward files a monthly count of the plants in that bed, with a dated photo and a seed sample in a numbered velvet pouch, and the two neighboring stewards countersign the count before it posts. Beds are finite, one per person, and a steward who misses two counts loses the bed to the waitlist. A thousand fake agents would need a thousand tended beds, a thousand monthly counts, and a thousand neighbors willing to sign for plants that do not exist.
